title: In the beginning (Genesis 1:1–5)
hookLine: the earth without form, the Spirit over the waters, and the first word: let there be light

lines: YEAR TWO: THE WHOLE BOOK, IN ORDER.
cards: The Bible doesn't open with a person. Before kings, prophets, a manger or a cross, there are three words in English: in the beginning.
And the road starts somewhere strange: in the dark, over deep water, before there's anything to see at all. Year one walked the hill in pieces: words, stories, practices, one Gospel, the depths.
Year two reads the whole book, in order, from the first line. Not every verse, but every turn of the road.

teach.b: In the King James Bible the first verse reads: "In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth." In Hebrew that opening phrase, in the beginning, is one word: bereshit.
In Jewish tradition it's also the name of the whole book.

Verse two sets the scene, and it isn't tidy: "And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep." In Hebrew, tohu va-vohu, a pair of words that sound like a shrug. Waste and empty.
But the same verse goes on: "And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters." The Hebrew word for Spirit, ruach, also means wind and breath. Some readers picture a bird hovering over a nest.
Something is about to happen. And then, up close, the first thing we see God do is speak.
"And God said, Let there be light: and there was light." No struggle, no battle, no raw material wrestled into shape.
A word, and light. God calls the light day and the darkness night, and the evening and the morning are the first day. The strange part: the sun doesn't arrive until day four.
Light comes before anything that shines.
Christians have read this in many ways, from a literal week to a poem about order coming out of chaos, and churches hold different views on how it fits with the science of the universe.
What they share is the opening claim: the world is made on purpose, by God. And Christians hear these words again at the start of John's Gospel: in the beginning was the Word.

how: Bible-in-a-year plans start with Genesis 1, and some churches read it at the Easter Vigil, where the story of creation is one of the first readings of the night.

games.q: the earth is without form and void, darkness over the deep. in the story, what is the first thing God does?
o: fights a sea monster to shape the world.
games.why: a word, and light. no struggle, no battle. the sun doesn't come until day four.

practice: Notice where the light in this room is coming from: a window, a lamp, a screen.
Close your eyes for a few breaths and rest in the dark behind your eyelids, then open them slowly and let the light come back in, as if for the first time.
If you pray, say the first line of the Bible quietly; if not, just watch the light arrive.

wordCard.voice: Bereshit. The Hebrew word that opens the Bible and names its first book: in the beginning, before anything had form.

orig.note: Hebrew: in the beginning, one word, the first in the Bible and the Jewish name for Genesis.

carryVoice: Your line: let there be light. A word first, and then everything else. Year two has begun.
